new='''Response bodies are capped at 64 MiB by default. Override globally with
`Config.MaxResponseSize`, per request with `WithResponseSizeLimit` or
`WithNoResponseSizeLimit`, and use `client.Files.DownloadTo` to stream large
v1 file downloads.

A request can only be retried when its body can be sent again. JSON bodies
always can. For request bodies you supply yourself (`Raw.Do`, `v1.Files.Add`,
`v1.Files.Update`, `v1.Persons.AddPicture`), a reader that implements
`io.ReaderAt` and `io.Seeker`, such as an `*os.File`, `*bytes.Reader` or
`*strings.Reader`, is replayed on retry. Any other reader is sent once and a
429 or 5xx response is returned as an error.

## File uploads

`client.Files.Upload` builds the `multipart/form-data` body for you from a
file name and an `io.Reader`, and links the file to an item through options.
The body is buffered before it is sent, so uploads retry like every other
call:

```go
f, err := os.Open("contract.pdf")
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
defer f.Close()

file, err := client.Files.Upload(
	context.Background(),
	filepath.Base(f.Name()),
	f,
	v1.WithFilesDealID(v1.DealID(123)),
)
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
log.Printf("uploaded file id=%d", file.ID)
```

`client.Files.Add` remains available when you need to build the request body
yourself.
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='CHANGELOG.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''## [Unreleased]

## [1.11.0] - 2026-08-18
'''
new='''## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Add `v1.Files.Upload`, which builds the `multipart/form-data` body from a
  file name and an `io.Reader`, with `WithFilesDealID`, `WithFilesPersonID`,
  `WithFilesOrganizationID`, `WithFilesProductID`, `WithFilesActivityID`,
  `WithFilesLeadID` and `WithFilesProjectID` to link the file to an item. The
  body is buffered before it is sent, so uploads are retried under the
  configured `RetryPolicy` like every other request.

### Fixed

- Request bodies that implement `io.ReaderAt` and `io.Seeker`, such as an
  `*os.File`, are now replayed on retry by `Raw.Do` and the v1 methods built on
  it (`Files.Add`, `Files.Update`, `Persons.AddPicture`). Only `*bytes.Reader`,
  `*bytes.Buffer` and `*strings.Reader` bodies could be resent before, so an
  upload read from an open file failed on the first 429 even with retries
  enabled. Such bodies are sent from their current offset with a
  `Content-Length` instead of chunked encoding, and each attempt reads through
  its own `io.SectionReader` so a late write from a rejected attempt cannot
  corrupt the retry. As before, a body that implements `io.Closer` is closed
  once the request completes.

## [1.11.0] - 2026-08-18
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(raw): replay seekable request bodies on retry

http.NewRequest only sets GetBody for *bytes.Reader, *bytes.Buffer and
*strings.Reader, so a body read from an *os.File was treated as
non-replayable and the retry transport returned the first 429 or 5xx
even with retries enabled.

RawClient.Do now gives bodies that implement io.ReaderAt and io.Seeker
a GetBody and a Content-Length. Each attempt reads through its own
io.SectionReader so a late write from a rejected attempt cannot corrupt
the retry, and the original body is closed once the request completes,
as net/http did before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

git add internal/multipartbody/multipartbody.go internal/multipartbody/multipartbody_test.go pipedrive/v1/files.go pipedrive/v1/files_test.go
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(v1): add Files.Upload with item link options

Files.Add required callers to build the multipart/form-data body
themselves. Files.Upload takes a file name and an io.Reader, like
CallLogs.AddRecording, and links the file to a deal, person,
organization, product, activity, lead or project through options.

The body is buffered, so uploads are retried like every other request.
multipartbody gains NewFileWithFields to write the link fields ahead of
the file part.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

text:
Both parts of the report are addressed on branch `fix/files-upload-retry`. The changes are verified but left uncommitted: no git identity is configured in this environment, and I did not want to invent one or edit your config. The exact commit commands are at the end.

**Root cause of the retry failure.** `Files.Add` hands your reader to `Raw.Do`, which builds the request with the standard library. The standard library only knows how to replay `*bytes.Reader`, `*bytes.Buffer` and `*strings.Reader` bodies. A body read from an open file has no replay hook, so the retry transport correctly refused to resend it and returned the first 429. The `RetryAllMethods` setting never came into play because 429 is retried for every method already.

**What changed**

- **`Raw.Do` replays seekable bodies.** Any body implementing both `io.ReaderAt` and `io.Seeker`, such as an open file, now gets a replay hook and a `Content-Length`. Each attempt reads through its own section reader rather than rewinding a shared one, so a server that rejects early cannot corrupt the retried body. The original body is still closed when the request finishes, as before. This fixes `Files.Add`, `Files.Update` and `Persons.AddPicture` without any API change.
- **New `Files.Upload(ctx, fileName, reader, opts...)`.** It builds the multipart body for you and mirrors `CallLogs.AddRecording`. Link options: `WithFilesDealID`, `WithFilesPersonID`, `WithFilesOrganizationID`, `WithFilesProductID`, `WithFilesActivityID`, `WithFilesLeadID`, `WithFilesProjectID`. The body is buffered, so it retries regardless of the reader type.
- **Docs.** README gains a file-upload section and a note on which bodies are retryable. CHANGELOG has Added and Fixed entries under Unreleased.

**Testing performed**

- New tests cover the reported scenario directly: a multipart body on disk passed to `Files.Add` retries after a 429, and `Files.Upload` retries with a one-shot reader.
- Unit tests for the replay helper check independent read…
